title: Concurrent collections
description: Choose the right concurrent collection for lock-free or low-contention scenarios in multithreaded code.

data.text: Standard collections like `List<T>` and `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` are not thread-safe. Adding or removing items while another thread reads or writes can corrupt data or throw exceptions. The `System.Collections.Concurrent` namespace provides collections designed for concurrent access.
Each concurrent collection is optimized for a specific access pattern. Choosing the wrong one can lead to unnecessary contention or poor performance.

rows: Lock-free reads; fine-grained locking for writes
Fast for adds/removes; iteration is a snapshot

data.title: Thread-safe cache with ConcurrentDictionary
Producer-consumer with BlockingCollection

items: Do not iterate a `ConcurrentBag` expecting a consistent snapshot — the collection may change during enumeration.
`GetConsumingEnumerable` blocks when the collection is empty and ends when `CompleteAdding` is called.
Concurrent collections reduce lock contention but do not eliminate the need for correct design.

data.title: Prefer concurrent collections over manual locking
data.text: If a standard concurrent collection fits your scenario, use it. Hand-rolled locking is error-prone and often slower than well-tested framework code.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Use `ConcurrentDictionary` for key-value caches and lookups.
Concurrent collections reduce but do not eliminate synchronization concerns.
